newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: PDVSA says Exxon $2 bln j-v talks speeding ahead.
newsitem.headline: PDVSA says Exxon $2 bln j-v talks speeding ahead.

text.p: Talks between U.S. oil giant Exxon and Venezuela's state-owned Petroleos de Venezuela (PDVSA) are advancing rapidly over a planned $2 billion joint venture to exploit extra heavy crude oil in Orinoco Tar belt, a PDVSA director said.

A letter of intent could be signed within three months, "and the project go to Congress for consideration in the third quarter of the year," Ronald Pantin, vice president of PDVSA affiliate Corpoven told reporters.
The project foresees production by two modules, of 80,000 barrels per day each, with operations beginning in 1999.
"It's a very aggressive project ... Exxon wants it to begin as soon as Congress agrees, with an investment of between $1.8 and $2 billion," Pantin said.
The extra heavy Orinoco crude will be treated in special deep conversion plants to lighten its gravity, and then shipped to Exxon plants in the U.S. for final refining.
Corpoven signed Wednesday a $3.5 billion extra heavy oil venture with Arco, Texaco and Phillips Petroleum.
